items.q: What does Ansor Edu do?
items.a: Ansor Edu is an educational consulting center that helps students gain admission to prestigious universities in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates on a full scholarship basis. We support you at every stage — from preparing documents to settling into your studies.

items.q: When was the company founded, and how much experience do you have?
items.a: Ansor Edu has been operating since 2022. During this time, hundreds of students have successfully enrolled in their dream universities on full scholarships.

items.q: Why should I choose Ansor Edu?
items.a: We offer experienced, certified consultants, partnerships with more than 10 universities, a 95% success rate, and full support from document preparation through graduation.

items.q: How is your success rate calculated?
items.a: 95% of students who contact us and submit all required documents in full are successfully admitted to their chosen university.

items.q: Which countries do you work with?
items.a: We currently work mainly with universities in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as with universities in Qatar.

items.q: Do you have proof of your track record?
items.a: Yes, you can read real student experiences in the "What Our Students Say" section of our website, and follow more success stories on our Telegram channel.

items.q: What does the full scholarship include?
items.a: The full scholarship covers round-trip flights, free accommodation, medical insurance, a monthly stipend, subsidized meals, free textbooks, local transportation, and excellence bonuses.

items.q: Is the scholarship really 100% free — are there any hidden costs?
items.a: The scholarship provided by the university is completely free — tuition, housing, and other essential costs are covered by the university. Ansor Edu's consulting service is billed separately; see the "Payment & Financial Matters" section for details.

items.q: How much is the monthly stipend?
items.a: The stipend amount varies by university and country. We'll give you the exact figure for your chosen university during your consultation.

items.q: What are the dormitories like?
items.a: Universities provide modern, comfortable dormitories for international students — usually rooms for 1-2 people with internet, air conditioning, and a shared kitchen.

items.q: How does the medical insurance work?
items.a: All scholarship students receive full medical insurance throughout their studies, covering hospital visits, medication, and emergency care.

items.q: Are flight costs covered?
items.a: Yes, round-trip flights — for arrival at the start of studies and departure after graduation — are fully covered by the university.

items.q: How is meal provision organized?
items.a: Students have access to a subsidized (discounted or free) meal system on campus, covering most of their daily food costs.

items.q: Are textbooks and study materials provided?
items.a: Yes, core textbooks and study materials are provided free of charge by the university library and faculty.

items.q: Are local transportation costs covered?
items.a: Yes, there are free or discounted transportation options both within the campus and, at some universities, for city transit as well.

items.q: What is the "excellence bonus"?
items.a: This is an additional financial reward or increased stipend given by the university to students who achieve outstanding academic results.

items.q: Which universities do you partner with?
items.a: We currently partner with more than 10 leading universities, including King Abdulaziz University, Umm Al-Qura University, the Islamic University of Madinah, King Saud University, KAUST, Princess Nora bint Abdulrahman University, Qassim University, Qatar University, and UAE University.

items.q: What is the international ranking of these universities?
items.a: Our partner universities rank among the world's top 150-800 according to the QS World University Rankings. The exact ranking for each university is listed on its page.

items.q: What fields of study are available?
items.a: A wide range of fields is available, including engineering, medicine, IT, Islamic studies, Arabic language, business, law, education, and social sciences. Each university has its own areas of strength.

items.q: Are there universities exclusively for women?
items.a: Yes, Princess Nora bint Abdulrahman University — the largest women's university in the world — offers full scholarship programs exclusively for female students.

items.q: Can I apply to several universities at the same time?
items.a: Yes, we recommend applying to several partner universities in parallel to increase your chances.

items.q: In which cities are the universities located?
items.a: The universities are located in Jeddah, Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, Buraydah (Saudi Arabia), Doha (Qatar), and Al-Ain (UAE).

items.q: Who can apply?
items.a: Any candidate who has completed secondary or vocational education and meets the requirements of their chosen university can apply.

items.q: Is there an age limit?
items.a: Most bachelor's programs recommend an age range of 17-25, though this can vary by university and program — we'll confirm the exact requirement during your consultation.

items.q: What GPA is required on my diploma/certificate?
items.a: The minimum required score varies from university to university; higher grades generally improve your admission chances. We'll tell you the exact requirement for your chosen university.

items.q: Is a language certificate required?
items.a: Some programs may require Arabic or English proficiency, but most universities offer a foundation year where the language is taught from scratch.

items.q: Is there an exam or interview?
items.a: Some universities may hold a short online interview or test. We'll let you know about this in advance during the application process and help you prepare.

items.q: Can I apply if I've studied abroad before?
items.a: Yes, we review such cases individually — during your consultation we'll assess your documents and suggest a suitable program.

items.q: Can I apply if I've just finished school?
items.a: Absolutely — most of our students are recent high school graduates. You can start the application process as soon as you receive your certificate.

items.q: Do you also help with master's or doctoral programs?
items.a: Yes, alongside bachelor's degrees, we also provide guidance for master's and, in some cases, doctoral programs.

items.q: What documents will I need?
items.a: You'll typically need a passport, your certificate/diploma with transcript, birth certificate, medical certificate, and photos. We provide the full list during your consultation.

items.q: Which documents need to be translated?
items.a: Core documents such as your certificate/diploma, birth certificate, and passport must be officially translated into Arabic or English and notarized. We take care of this entire process for you.

items.q: Where is notarization done?
items.a: Document notarization is carried out through local (Uzbekistan/Kyrgyzstan) notary offices, and we provide full assistance throughout this process.

items.q: How long must my passport be valid?
items.a: Your passport should be valid for at least 1.5-2 years, since the application and visa process takes some time.

items.q: Is a medical certificate required?
items.a: Yes, most universities require a general medical certificate, which may include test results for certain infectious diseases.

items.q: Is a certificate of no criminal record required?
items.a: Some universities and visa types may require a certificate confirming you have no criminal record. We'll give you the exact list during your consultation.

items.q: Can I apply if I don't know Arabic?
items.a: Yes, you don't need to know Arabic. Most universities offer a foundation year, where Arabic is taught from the beginning.

items.q: Is there a language preparation year at university?
items.a: Yes, most of our partner universities offer a one-year language and academic preparation program to get students ready for their main faculty.

items.q: Is an IELTS/TOEFL certificate required?
items.a: It's not required for most programs, since the foundation year covers language training. Some special programs taught in English may require a language certificate.

items.q: Is teaching in Arabic or in English?
items.a: Most programs are taught in Arabic, though some technical and medical fields also offer programs taught in English.

items.q: How long does the process take after I apply?
items.a: Once all documents are submitted, it usually takes 1-3 months to receive a response from the university, depending on the institution and the season.

items.q: When will I receive the university's admission decision?
items.a: Admission decisions usually arrive within a few weeks of applying, though it can take up to 2-3 months depending on the university's process.

items.q: Can I reapply if my application is rejected?
items.a: Yes, we analyze the reasons for rejection and help you reapply in the next intake or to another partner university.

items.q: When does the application period start and end?
items.a: Deadlines vary by university, and admissions are usually announced once or twice a year, for the fall and spring semesters. We'll let you know the exact dates.

items.q: How many intakes are there per year?
items.a: Most universities have 1-2 intakes per year, mainly for the fall semester, with some also offering a spring semester intake.

items.q: Can I still apply after the deadline has passed?
items.a: In some cases, late admission spots may become available. Contact us after the deadline to ask about current opportunities.

items.q: How do you help with the visa process?
items.a: Once you receive your university acceptance letter, we provide full support in preparing and submitting all the documents needed for your student visa.

items.q: How long does it take to get a visa?
items.a: A student visa is usually processed within 2-6 weeks, though this can vary depending on the embassy's workload.

items.q: What preparation is provided before departure?
items.a: Before departure, we hold a pre-departure briefing covering culture, climate, essential items to bring, and everything you need to know for your first days.

items.q: Is there an airport pickup service?
items.a: Most universities offer an airport pickup service for new students and transport to campus.

items.q: Do you provide support after arrival too?
items.a: Yes, our post-arrival support covers settling in, registration, and help during the initial adjustment period.

items.q: Who can I contact if I have a problem during my studies?
items.a: Our team stays in touch throughout your studies — you can reach out to us anytime via Telegram with your questions.

items.q: Can students work while studying?
items.a: Some countries and visa types allow limited part-time work, depending on local law and university regulations.

items.q: Do you help graduates find jobs?
items.a: Most universities have career centers that help graduates find employment, and our alumni network can also provide useful connections.

items.q: What's the climate like in Saudi Arabia/UAE?
items.a: The climate is generally hot and dry, with high temperatures in summer. University campuses and dormitories are all equipped with air conditioning.

items.q: Do I need to follow local culture and customs?
items.a: Yes, respecting the host country's laws and traditions is important. We cover this in detail during the pre-departure briefing.

items.q: Will I have trouble finding halal food?
items.a: No, all food in Saudi Arabia and the UAE meets halal standards, so this isn't something to worry about.

items.q: How safe are these countries?
items.a: Saudi Arabia and the UAE are among the safest countries in the world, with very low crime rates.

items.q: Is there an Uzbek/Kyrgyz student community?
items.a: Yes, many universities have a Central Asian student community that helps new students settle in.

items.q: What does the medical insurance cover?
items.a: Insurance typically covers general checkups, emergency care, and the costs of basic treatment. Exact terms vary by university.

items.q: Do I need to pay extra to visit a hospital?
items.a: No extra payment is required for services covered by insurance, though services outside its coverage may involve a fee.

items.q: Are medication costs covered?
items.a: In most cases, basic medications are covered under the medical insurance plan.

items.q: How much do your services cost?
items.a: The cost depends on the package of services you choose. We'll give you an exact price during your free, personalized consultation.

items.q: Is the consultation free?
items.a: Yes, the initial consultation is completely free — during it, we assess your chances and explain the next steps.

items.q: When is payment made?
items.a: Payment is usually made in stages — part at the start of document preparation, and the rest once admission is confirmed.

items.q: Is there a refund policy?
items.a: If a university issues an unjustified rejection, a partial refund may be considered under the terms of your contract. Exact conditions are specified in the contract.

items.q: What payment methods are available?
items.a: You can pay by cash, bank transfer, or card.

items.q: Can I pay in foreign currency?
items.a: Yes, payment can be made in local currency or US dollars — this can be arranged during your consultation.

items.q: Do you sign a contract?
items.a: Yes, before starting our services we sign a bilateral contract that clearly outlines all services, timelines, and payment terms.

items.q: Will I receive a receipt?
items.a: Yes, you will receive an official document (receipt) for every payment.

items.q: Are there special arrangements for women?
items.a: Yes, there are separate dormitories for female students, and some universities — such as Princess Nora bint Abdulrahman University — are exclusively for women.

items.q: Are there facilities for religious practice?
items.a: Yes, campuses have prayer spaces and mosques, providing everything needed for religious practice.

items.q: Can siblings apply together?
items.a: Yes, family members can apply separately, and we work with each candidate individually.

items.q: Can married students apply?
items.a: Yes, marital status doesn't prevent you from applying. Some universities also offer housing options for married students.

items.q: Are there accommodations for students with disabilities?
items.a: Many modern campuses have infrastructure adapted for students with special needs. We'll check the specific options for your chosen university.

items.q: Can I get a scholarship for a second degree?
items.a: Some programs are open to second-degree students, though this depends on the university's policy. We'll review your individual case during a consultation.

items.q: How many years does the scholarship cover?
items.a: For bachelor's programs, the scholarship usually covers the entire course of study (4-6 years, depending on the major).

items.q: What GPA do I need to keep my scholarship?
items.a: Universities generally require satisfactory academic performance. The exact minimum GPA depends on university policy, and we'll explain this in detail during the preparation period.

items.q: Will my scholarship be canceled if my GPA drops?
items.a: If low performance continues for a long period, the university will issue a warning and give you time to improve. Cancellation is usually a last resort.

items.q: Can I change my major?
items.a: Most universities allow you to choose or change your major during the first (foundation) year.

items.q: Is it possible to transfer to another university?
items.a: This is rare and depends on university policy. If needed, we'll provide individual guidance.

items.q: What makes you different from other education consulting companies?
items.a: Our advantage is direct communication with partner universities, a transparent process, an experienced team, and a 95% success rate.

items.q: Can't I apply directly without an agency?
items.a: In theory, yes, but properly preparing documents, arranging translation, notarization, and communicating with the university is a complex, time-consuming process. We take that burden off your shoulders and reduce the risk of errors.

items.q: How can I protect myself from fraud?
items.a: We operate under an official contract, all payments are documented, and we can put you in touch with our real students.

items.q: Where can I read reviews and feedback?
items.a: You can find genuine feedback from our students in the "What Our Students Say" section of our website and on our Telegram/Instagram pages.

items.q: Do I apply online, or do I need to visit an office?
items.a: You can submit your application entirely online through the "Contact" section of our website. Our specialist will then get in touch with you for the next steps.

items.q: Is the information I submit through the website secure?
items.a: Yes, all information submitted through the form is kept confidential and used only for the application process.

items.q: Can I correct my information if I made a mistake in the form?
items.a: Of course — just contact us via Telegram or phone, and we'll help you update your information.

items.q: How can I get a consultation?
items.a: Fill out the "Submit Application" form on our website, or message us directly on Telegram (@ansor_edu_admin) — we'll get in touch for a free consultation.

items.q: Can I reach you via Telegram?
items.a: Yes, you can ask us questions anytime through our Telegram account @ansor_edu_admin.

items.q: How is the free consultation conducted?
items.a: The consultation can be held by phone call, Telegram chat, or video call — whichever is most convenient for you.

items.q: What are your working hours?
items.a: We work Monday through Friday, from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM.
